channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [7] Imaging of gate-controlled suppression of superconductivity via the Meissner effect
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: A. Di Bernardo, C. L. Degen

Authors: K. J. Knapp, U. Ognjanović, P. J. Scheidegger, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of gate-controlled superconductivity via Meissner effect, relevant to quantum materials.

Tags: #superconductivity #scanningprobemicroscopy #quantummaterials

Abstract: Supercurrents flowing through thin superconducting nanowires can be quenched by applying a gate voltage, an effect known as gate-controlled suppression of superconductivity. Here, using a scanning nitrogen-vacancy magnetometer at sub-Kelvin temperatures, the authors report that this phenomenon also manifests in a suppression of Meissner screening and is thus not restricted to transport.
